questionText: Consider a computer system with DMA support. The DMA module is transferring one 8-bit character in one CPU cycle from a device to memory through cycle stealing at regular intervals. Consider a $2\text{ MHz}$ processor. If $0.5\%$ processor cycles are used for DMA, the data transfer rate of the device is _________ bits per second.
explanation:
Given Data:
• Processor clock frequency = $2\text{ MHz} = 2 \times 10^6\text{ cycles/second}$
• Data transferred per DMA cycle = $1\text{ character} = 8\text{ bits}$
• Percentage of processor cycles used for DMA = $0.5\%$

Step 1: Calculate total DMA cycles per second.
$\text{DMA cycles per second} = 0.5\% \times (2 \times 10^6) = \frac{0.5}{100} \times 2,000,000 = 10,000\text{ cycles/second}$

Step 2: Calculate the data transfer rate in bits per second.
Since each cycle transfers $8\text{ bits}$:
$\text{Data Transfer Rate} = 10,000\text{ cycles/second} \times 8\text{ bits/cycle} = 80,000\text{ bits per second}$

Hence, the correct answer is 80000.
